content:
CNN chief data analyst Harry Enten mocked Sen. John Fetterman’s (Pa.) threat to leave the Democratic Party, pointing to a brutal polling detail that suggests Pennsylvania Democrats might be thrilled to see him go.

On Monday’s broadcast of “CNN News Central,” host John Berman noted that Fetterman’s warning that he could quit the party if Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.) is elected Senate majority leader “may be landing a little differently” following Democrats’ massive gains in the 2026 midterm elections.

Fetterman, a frequent guest on conservative Fox News, has increasingly broken with Democrats on multiple issues, and has criticized Van Hollen as “very anti-, hostile to Israel.”

With a larger Senate majority, Democrats now “don’t necessarily need” Fetterman’s vote as much as they once did, Berman suggested.

Enten agreed, joking that Democrats’ reaction to the prospect of Fetterman leaving the party could be summed up by a LeBron James meme: “Oooh, I’m really scared. Oh no.”

“They would say good riddance, good riddance to this guy,” he added.

Enten then highlighted polling data that “says it all.”

Fetterman’s net favorability among Pennsylvania Democrats stood at a positive 56 percentage points in November 2024. Two years later, it had plunged to negative 56 points.

“It’s literally the inverse now,” Enten said. “That is a change of … 112 points in the negative direction … in just two years’ time.”

“Pennsylvania Democrats despise, they hate, hate, hate John Fetterman,” he continued. “So this idea that he would move and make their majority go from 56 seats to 55 seats, ooooh, real scary.”
